action_items.item: Roll out flags such as monthly-spend-feature in stages, with an automatic rollback when latency on the affected pages rises above baseline.
Alert on a rise in account-page latency sooner, so the page arrives close to the onset instead of {alert_raised - began} later.
Make the change-event timestamp for flag toggles agree with the flag evaluation logs. The toggle event was recorded after logs already showed the flag on, which slowed correlation.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers saw slow account pages on io-shop from {began} to {recovered}. The latency series the alert watches rose from {series_before} to {series_while_broken} on average, peaking at {series_at_worst}. The error rate rose slightly, from {errors_before} to {errors_while_broken}.

From {began} nearly every request evaluated monthly-spend-feature as on. The first evaluations at the onset were {G971b.3} on and {G971b.2} off out of {G971b.4}, and the flag stayed on for every logged evaluation afterwards. Before that, the flag was off and account pages rendered normally.
The flag was switched on by an admin. This was the only production change in the window, and no deploy happened.

The feature path behind the flag made affected account-page requests much slower. Reverting the flag to off brought the service back to its baseline from {recovered}, and the rule that paged stopped firing. This confirms the flag as the trigger.
The evidence stops here. It does not show why the feature path is slow. A draft code fix has been proposed but not yet reviewed or merged.

contributing_factors.factor: The flag could be switched on for all traffic with no staged rollout and no automatic latency check. A feature with severe tail latency reached nearly all requests within a minute.
The alert fired {alert_raised - began} after the onset, so shoppers were affected before anyone was paged.
The slow path in the feature code is still unfixed, and the flag is only held off, so re-enabling it would bring the slowdown back.

input.executive_summary: For {duration}, from {began} to {recovered}, some shoppers on io-shop found account pages slow, and a small share of requests failed. The error rate went from {errors_before} to {errors_while_broken} on average, peaking at {errors_at_worst}. The slowdown started when the monthly-spend-feature flag was switched on. Argus linked the slowdown to that change and switched the flag back off. Metrics were back at baseline from {recovered}, and the response was confirmed {closed} after being held for {held}. A draft pull request with a code fix has been proposed and still needs review.

got_lucky: The feature hurt latency far more than it hurt correctness, so the error rate rose only slightly, to {errors_at_worst} at worst.
The flag could be reverted instantly without a deploy. A feature without a kill switch would have taken much longer to undo.
went_well: Argus tied the onset to the flag change within minutes and reverted the flag.
The revert was verified against the service's own metrics before the incident was closed as mitigated.
A draft code-fix pull request was proposed straight after mitigation.
went_wrong: The slowdown was live for {duration} before the revert took effect.
The paging alert came {alert_raised - began} after the onset.
The flag-toggle change event is stamped after the evaluation logs already showed the flag on, so the record is inconsistent about when the change happened.

input.root_cause: Enabling the monthly-spend-feature flag on io-shop sent account-page requests down a feature path that added severe tail latency. The record shows the flag going on and latency recovering once it was reverted, but it does not show what inside the feature path is slow.
input.symptom: Account pages were slow and some requests failed
